acceptance.given: A Toolchain write operation is proposed against each protected Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, and user-sandbox path category.

oracle.expected: Every attempted write is deterministically rejected, leaves the target unchanged, and reports a boundary violation; the same enforcement applies across all five protected categories.
forbidden: Any Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, or user-sandbox file is modified under this scope.
oracle.observable: The boundary validator returns a rejection for each protected-path fixture and byte/state comparison confirms no protected file changed.

acceptance.then: The protected-path boundary check is evaluated before any filesystem mutation is permitted.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain boundary validator is executed against the protected-path fixtures.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the protected-path negative validator to demonstrate that a proposed write to a Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, or user-sandbox path is accepted instead of rejected.
Use the protected-path negative validator to detect any protected target whose bytes or existence changed after the attempted write.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a Toolchain-only, fail-closed write boundary: before filesystem mutation, classify repository-relative targets and reject all Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, and user-sandbox paths while preserving protected-target bytes and state. The check must not authorize or modify Phase service or sandbox code.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback removes only the boundary-enforcement change and preserves existing receipt, schema, and lifecycle semantics; no protected path or live database state is altered.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed write -> protected-path classification -> deterministic rejection with no mutation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All five protected path categories produce rejection results and byte/state checks show no protected target changed; any accepted write or mutation is a failed terminal result.

acceptance.given: A candidate and a validator capability with its source, content, semantic dependencies, compatibility, support policy, and scope are available for evaluation.

oracle.expected: An independent verification establishes candidate-external trust from the bound validator capability and complete dependency closure rather than another verification's conclusion.
forbidden: Trust inferred solely from another verification
oracle.observable: The validator evaluation result exposes an independently verified candidate-external trust binding.

acceptance.when: The validator evaluation selector evaluates the candidate and its bound validator capability.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Supply candidate-controlled or incomplete trust bindings and observe the independent trust check reject them.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Independently evaluate candidate-external validator trust against bound source, content, dependency, compatibility, policy, and scope identities.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Untrusted or candidate-controlled bindings fail closed and do not become trust authority.

slice_hint.state_transition: Candidate trust unverified -> independently verified candidate-external trust or rejected evaluation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The evaluation independently binds candidate-external trust and rejects omitted, inherited-only, candidate-controlled, or incomplete trust verification.

acceptance.given: An applicable Consumer has completed enable, disable, and behavioral rollback through its applicable route sequence.

oracle.expected: The applicable Consumer invokes the current approved Candidate Route through its real call surface and exposes the resulting re-enable execution.
oracle.observable: A real Consumer call surface records or exposes successful re-enable execution.

acceptance.then: Re-enable has been executed by the applicable Consumer through a real call surface.
acceptance.when: After disable and behavioral rollback, re-enable is exercised for the applicable Consumer.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use a skip or simulated-call condition and observe that re-enable cannot be accepted without a real Consumer Candidate-Route call.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each applicable Consumer to re-enable by invoking the current approved Candidate Route through its real call surface and capture that call's result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Re-enable remains a Candidate-Route invocation after the prior disable and rollback sequence; configuration-only switching is insufficient.

slice_hint.state_transition: Applicable Consumer after behavioral rollback -> real Candidate-Route re-enable call recorded.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every applicable Consumer's re-enable transition invokes the real Candidate Route and exposes its current execution result.

acceptance.given: Validator evaluation is prepared for a repository Toolchain package, with validator content, semantic-dependency inputs, support policy, and scope available for candidate-external binding.

oracle.expected: Before evaluation, scripts/sc/skill_package_replay.py constructs a candidate-external trust envelope containing immutable identities for validator content, every semantic-dependency member, support policy, and scope; replay proceeds only when the envelope is complete and unchanged.
forbidden: The candidate supplies, selects, or mutates the trust envelope or any trusted member.
A missing, ambiguous, or changed validator, dependency, support-policy, or scope member is accepted as valid.
Evaluation proceeds without an independently attributable pre-evaluation envelope.
oracle.observable: The replay receipt and validator trace expose the envelope authority boundary, complete member identity set, and deterministic invalidation result for missing, ambiguous, or mutated members.

acceptance.then: A complete unchanged candidate-external trust envelope is accepted for evaluation; any incomplete, ambiguous, candidate-controlled, or drifted envelope is rejected before evaluation.
acceptance.when: Immediately before validator evaluation and again at the trust-binding gate after dependency and policy identities are resolved.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate validator content or a semantic-dependency member after envelope creation; the replay must emit an invalid/stale trust-envelope terminal result before evaluation.
Remove or make ambiguous one required envelope member; the pre-evaluation gate must reject without producing a successful evaluation result.
Supply the envelope from candidate-controlled input or substitute candidate-reported identities; trust establishment must be rejected as non-external.

affected_subjects: candidate-external validator trust envelope construction and validation
slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or repair the pre-evaluation trust-envelope gate in scripts/sc/skill_package_replay.py so it freezes validator content identity, the complete semantic-dependency closure, support policy, and scope from the repository-authoritative path, and deterministically invalidates on missing, ambiguous, candidate-controlled, or changed members.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay CLI and receipt schemas; rollback removes only the trust-envelope repair while retaining prior non-authorizing behavior and fail-closed terminal categories.

slice_hint.state_transition: unbound -> candidate-external envelope assembled -> complete/unchanged accepted OR missing/ambiguous/changed/candidate-controlled rejected before evaluation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Terminal success is permitted only when the envelope authority is candidate-external and every validator, semantic-dependency, support-policy, and scope identity matches the frozen pre-evaluation binding; otherwise the terminal result is invalid-input, identity-invalid, or stale and no evaluation result is accepted.
